sections.content: *Is* means “too” or “also”. It stands right after the word it adds to, and the sentence is about that word: *Anna is tanul* means “Anna studies too”, so someone else studies and Anna joins them.

sections.title: Move is, move the “too”
rows: I read in the morning too.

sections.title: Two people
sections.content: When two people share the verb, *is* comes after the pair: *Meg és Károly is főznek.* (Meg and Károly cook too.)

items.english: We walk in the afternoon too.

sections.content: English puts “too” at the end: “I read too.” In Hungarian, first decide which word gets the “too”, then put *is* right after it. Never start a sentence with *is*.
